customManagers.description: Update ARGs annotated with '# renovate: datasource=… depName=…'. Needed because the base images compose multiple ARGs in FROM (e.g. ${REGISTRY_DOCKERHUB}/library/rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm), which the dockerfile manager cannot auto-replace. Two matchStrings because ARGs come in two shapes, and the digest has to be captured SEPARATELY: the original single pattern captured '0.3.2@sha256:…' as one currentValue, which no versioning scheme can parse — so every digest-pinned ARG in the repo (cve-gate's three bases, ci-runner's CVE_GATE_VERSION and RUNNER_VERSION) was silently unmanaged. First pattern: ARGs whose value ends ':<tag>@<digest>' or is '<version>@<digest>'. Second: bare versions with no digest, digest-containing values excluded so the two patterns never both match.

Update tool versions that composite actions pass as INPUT DEFAULTS (syft, cosign). Renovate's action manager pins the `uses:` ref but is blind to a version string handed to that action via `with:` — which is how syft sat on v1.21.0 from 2026-06-16 until v1.48.0 shipped, with nothing watching it.

packageRules.description: Patch and minor updates do not need a dashboard tick in this repo. The org preset (webgrip/renovate-config) puts dependencyDashboardApproval on EVERY update type, which is right where a bump ships straight to production. Here it does not: build-check builds every changed image on the PR, and the release path runs the image against its cve-budgets.yaml entry before it can publish. The tick therefore adds a human step without adding a check — and 31 of them had accumulated, which is worse than no gate, because a queue nobody works is indistinguishable from a queue with nothing important in it. Majors, rollbacks and replacements KEEP the gate: helm v4, cosign v3 and Node 22/24 are migrations, not bumps, and the preset's prConcurrentLimit of 5 still caps how many land at once.

These Dockerfiles compose their FROM refs from multiple ARGs; the dockerfile manager resolves the ARGs at extraction but then cannot find the resolved string in the raw file ('Cannot find replaceString' → the whole branch silently produces no commit). The annotated-ARG custom manager above owns these deps instead.

The release toolchain (webgrip/workflows ADR-0005) is the one npm dependency set in this repo that is LOCKED, because it decides every repo's version numbers. These package.json files are also their image's release manifest — Renovate owns the dependencies; semantic-release owns the version. It upgrades as ONE reviewed PR across all three images — they must stay on the same semantic-release version, since the derived images replace the base's tree wholesale. A MAJOR bump is expected to FAIL the image build: each Dockerfile asserts the major that webgrip/workflows' composites target. The group bypasses the repository's PR and branch concurrency limits: on 2026-10-23 @webgrip/semantic-release-config 1.4.0 (the forge adapter homelab ADR-0069 requires) sat behind the preset's prConcurrentLimit of 5, so no toolchain image shipped it and only Ploeg released with it.
Annotated ARGs hold bare versions that are reused outside the FROM line (rustup default, tag suffix composition); appending @sha256 digests would corrupt them.

techdocs-builder's python env is pip-compile hash-locked (requirements*.in -> .txt, compiled for python:3.13-alpine). Renovate re-runs the header command to refresh locks+hashes. mkdocs-techdocs-core pins most of the mkdocs universe with == constraints, so most transitive 'updates' are impossible until techdocs-core itself bumps — expect small PRs. zensical lives in a SEPARATE lock (requirements-zensical) because it cannot coexist with techdocs-core (pymdown-extensions conflict).

laya-serve's python env is pip-compile hash-locked in two steps, mirroring the two installs it replaced (VIK-2308): requirements-torch.in resolves torch and its dependencies from the PyTorch CPU index alone, and requirements.in resolves laya[serve] against that lock as a constraint file. Compiled inside the image's python:3.12-debian13 build base.

Lock file maintenance changes what an image installs, so it must cut that image's release. The org preset commits it as chore(deps), which semantic-release ignores: the refreshed lock would sit on main and no image would ever carry it. Every ops/docker/<image>/tools/*/package-lock.json and pip-compile lock is installed into its image at build time (VIK-2308).

webgrip/workflows is pinned by commit SHA with a '# main' branch annotation — the repo cuts no tags, so Renovate's tag lookup 404s (GET /repos/webgrip/workflows/tags/main) and the FATAL aborts the ENTIRE repo run, taking every other update (including all annotated-ARG bumps) down with it. The pin is moved deliberately by hand when the reusables change; Renovate has nothing to version here.
